Appellant-Vishal Saxena has filed this appeal under Section 14-A(2) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 to challenge the impugned order dated 06.05.2024 passed by the Special Judge, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, Moradabad in Special Sessions Trial No. 910 of 2018, titled State Vs. Vishal Saxena,
arising out of Case Crime No. 979 of2016, under Section 506 IPC and Section 3(1)(X) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, Police Station Civil Lines, District Moradabad has been rejected.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant has pointed out that the said summoning order dated 16.11.2017 was challenged before this Court through application bearing no. 2214 of 2018 and while refusing to interfere with the summoning order dated 16.11.2017, liberty was granted to the appellant to move a discharge application.
Learned counsel submits that pursuant to the said liberty, the appellant preferred a discharge application and the same has been partly accepted order dated 08.04.2023.

Learned counsel has pointed out that in this background, it is a fit case for grant of concession of pre-arrest bail to the appellant, but ignoring the facts and circumstances, the Special Judge,
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act vide impugned order dated 06.05.2024 has proceeded to decline his pre-arrest bail.
The prayer is opposed by learned counsel for the complainant, who referred to the impugned order dated 06.05.2024 and submitted that in view of Section 18 of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, the application seeking pre-arrest bail is not maintainable,
therefore, the Special Judge, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,
Moradabad has rightly rejected the same.
This Court does not find any merit in this appeal as initially the FIR was registered against the appellant on 28.08.2016 and no application seeking pre-arrest bail was ever filed by the appellant,
much less after passing of the summoning order dated 16.11.2017.

sentences.text: During the course of hearing, learned counsel for the appellant fairly stated that as the appellant was granted liberty to move a discharge application, therefore, the appellant did not file any application under Section 438 Cr.P.C.

That apart, according to learned counsel after filing the discharge application, the appellant has been appearing before the Special Judge, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, therefore, considering the above background,
particularly the delay in seeking the concession of pre-arrest bail, that too after submitting himself before the trial court pursuant to issuance of process dated 16.11.2017, this Court is not inclined to exercise the appellate powers.
